big: An IPO states a price band of ₹180 to ₹190. Meena wants 70 shares. She does not know the final price. The system lets her bid, and block her money, without paying until she is allotted shares.

lines: If I do not know the final price, how much do I bid?
You can bid at the cut-off, which means you accept whatever final price is set within the band. Your bank blocks the money for the upper price, and releases any extra later.

rows: ₹12,950 is used, the rest is released
note: With ASBA through UPI, the money stays in your account, blocked, and is debited only if shares are allotted.

q: Rohan applies at cut-off in an IPO with a band of ₹180 to ₹190. What does he agree to?
opts: Any final price in the band
Only the price of ₹180 a share
Only the price of ₹190 a share
Any price that he likes best
why: Cut-off means he accepts whatever final price is set within the band.
He is not tied to the lower end, since the price may be higher.
The final price may be lower than the upper end.
The price must fall within the band, and it is not his to choose.

q: Meena applies using ASBA with UPI. When is her money actually debited?
why: At application the money is only blocked, not taken.
If no shares are allotted, the block is released without debit.
The amount is blocked and debited only on allotment.
If she is allotted shares, the money is debited.

why: It has nothing to do with writing a book about the firm.

q: The band is ₹180 to ₹190. Meena wants 70 shares at the upper price. How much is blocked?
why: ₹12,600 would be 70 shares at ₹180, the lower end.
₹190 is the price of one share, not for 70.
₹70 is the number of shares and not the amount.

pts: Cut-off: you accept the final price set within the band.
ASBA with UPI blocks money and debits it only on allotment.
